utterances.text: I wasn't allowed to move around certain areas at all. I had a set route that I was able to move around in, but not elsewhere.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: Well, apparently you moved around the restaurant because on the cross-examination, you said that you would see some guards slap and kick the detainees when they went to eat. So you saw some people, after all, being beaten?

utterances.speaker: CEDO VULETA
utterances.text: They did slap them and kick them. I saw that. Yes, I did see that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: Don't you call that beating? Because at first you said you never saw beating. So you saw beating?

utterances.speaker: CEDO VULETA
utterances.text: Well, it wasn't the kind of beating that would lead to serious injury.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: So it wasn't serious beating. And you said that at that time Mr. Gruban told the guards not to kick the detainees and let them be in peace, but the detainees did not obey him; is that right?

utterances.speaker: CEDO VULETA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: You also mentioned that when people were coming out of the bus, the detainees coming out of the bus, Mr. Kvocka opened his wide shirt and told them not to shoot the people. He said, "They are people. They are people here." And you said that he was obeyed. Was that right?

utterances.speaker: CEDO VULETA
utterances.text: I wasn't on the spot when this happened, but I heard about it from my fellow workers, that this incident had occurred and that Kvocka stood in front of this column of people.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: And they told you that he was obeyed, as you said?

utterances.speaker: CEDO VULETA
utterances.text: I don't know. The shooting stopped, that's what the other workers told me, but I wasn't on the spot.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: Did you know about this incident? Because you said he opened his shirt wide. What does that mean, "Shoot me instead of them," or what? Why did he open his shirt wide?

utterances.speaker: CEDO VULETA
utterances.text: Well, that's what I heard from the others. I didn't actually see it myself.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: I mean, he would risk his life to protect the detainees? Was that the image?

utterances.speaker: CEDO VULETA
utterances.text: Well, yes, that seems to be the whole image, to prevent a greater catastrophe from happening.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: And he was obeyed? They stopped? They stopped the shooting?

utterances.speaker: CEDO VULETA
utterances.text: The shooting stopped. Whether they obeyed him or not, I can't say.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: The shooting -- yes, yes. That's all my questions, thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Judge Fouad Riad. Madam Judge Wald has the floor.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WALD
utterances.text: Mr. Vuleta, you were at the camp, you told us, from the end of May to the beginning of August, is that right, when it closed?

utterances.speaker: CEDO VULETA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WALD
utterances.text: And you did have occasion, from your testimony, at some times to see groups of detainees, either as you went about your work or you mentioned the specific incident of seeing them on their way to lunch. My question to you is, over that period of time, did the detainees that you saw look like healthy, well-nourished males? I mean, did they look like the employees of the camp -- of the mine or the guards? Did they look healthy over the period? Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: CEDO VULETA
utterances.text: In that period there were people who looked completely healthy. Other elderly people didn't look so well. There were some people that were sick. There were other people that were naturally slim. Other people were fat.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WALD
utterances.text: But was your impression over that period of time that the detainees that you saw overall looked like average people you would have seen on the street, or they looked thinner, more -- less healthy, more ragged, dirty, sick?

utterances.speaker: CEDO VULETA
utterances.text: They looked dirtier. They didn't have the necessary hygienic conditions or the food that they would have liked to have had. They looked like prisoners, not like people parading around in town.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WALD
utterances.text: Okay. Now, you mentioned that the cleaning women who were employees of the mine, to your knowledge, were used to clean the kitchens and some parts of holding quarters -- well, no, I'm sorry, that they were used to clean the kitchens and some parts of the administration building. To your knowledge, to your knowledge, did those cleaning women, those women who were mine employees, were they ever used, to your knowledge, to go into the other buildings where the detainees were to do any cleaning, the hangars or the bathrooms or the places where the prisoners slept, to your knowledge? Do you know if they were used to ever do any cleaning in the parts of the compound where the prisoners stayed?

utterances.speaker: CEDO VULETA
utterances.text: I saw the cleaning ladies mostly in the kitchen, the administrative building, the restaurant where the food was handed out. I didn't notice them in the toilets or the hangar where the detainees were put up.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WALD
utterances.text: Okay. Now, you mentioned earlier on that you were aware of a security group from Banja Luka, soldiers, I think, but from Banja Luka, who were doing some of the guarding at the camp. My question to you is, was that true during the entire period that you were in the camp, or was that true only for a short time after you came to the camp, that you were aware of the presence that you mentioned of the Banja Luka -- not the interrogators, but the Banja Luka security guards. Were they there the whole time you were in the camp, or only for a portion of that time?

utterances.speaker: CEDO VULETA
utterances.text: They were only there for part of the time. I don't know exactly what date they left.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WALD
utterances.text: Never mind the exact date, but was that the early part of the camp that you were there or the later part of the camp?

utterances.speaker: CEDO VULETA
utterances.text: The earlier part.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WALD
utterances.text: Now, my last question to you is we talked a lot about the drinking water supply system and the industrial water which you said was used for both pumping the mines and for washing down trucks. My only question -- I think you said that. No?

utterances.speaker: CEDO VULETA
utterances.text: There was different water being pumped out from the hole, from the pit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WALD
utterances.text: I understand.

utterances.speaker: CEDO VULETA
utterances.text: The other water was separate. So the industrial water came from the Gomjenica River.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WALD
utterances.text: My question to you is: You mentioned that this industrial or non-drinking water was attached by pumps and it was used sometimes to wash trucks. Was that -- my question is: Was that source of water, the non-drinking water supply system, the source of water that would be used to wash down trucks or that sort of thing, was that accessible to the guards? I mean, was that in a place where guards could go to it and take it if they wanted to? I'm not saying what they used it for. I'm just asking you, was it in a place that was accessible to the guards?

utterances.speaker: CEDO VULETA
utterances.text: That place was accessible to the guards, but the water could not function until the pumps had been switched on because it is extremely high pressure and would knock a man down if water were to be pumped out that way.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WALD
utterances.text: So does your answer mean that you would have to be notified or you would have to know about it if they wanted to turn that water on for some reason, for whatever reason?

utterances.speaker: CEDO VULETA
utterances.text: I didn't have to be informed, notified. There were people handling it. There was a switch off/switch on mechanism.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WALD
utterances.text: So the last part of that question is, you said several times, I think, that nobody could drink that industrial water. I mean, it just was not fit for drinking. My question is: Was that because of the taste or what? I know it's not healthy for them, but you made a very strong statement. "Nobody would ever touch that." "Nobody could drink that." Was that because the taste was so bad that they couldn't physically drink it or why?

utterances.speaker: CEDO VULETA
utterances.text: The water couldn't be drunk because of the taste. It's dirty water. Not even the livestock, the cattle, would drink it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WALD
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much, Judge Wald. Mr. Vuleta, I too have a few questions for you. You told us that at one point in time, you asked the detainees to help you repair something. Did I understand you correctly?

utterances.speaker: CEDO VULETA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And the manager brought them to you. Who was that manager?

utterances.speaker: CEDO VULETA
utterances.text: It was Mirko Babic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] He was the manager of what?

utterances.speaker: CEDO VULETA
utterances.text: He was the manager of the workshop which was used for maintenance of mining machinery.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Thank you. You also told us that there were locations which were inaccessible to you.

utterances.speaker: CEDO VULETA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] What were those locations?

utterances.speaker: CEDO VULETA
utterances.text: I could not enter the premises where detainees were put up. During the night, I was not allowed to be outside. I had to go to my workshop, to sleep there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If there was a power failure on one of the locations where the detainees were accommodated, what would happen? How would you go about that particular damage?

utterances.speaker: CEDO VULETA
utterances.text: If there was a breakdown, then my superior would notify me about that breakdown, and I would go to that particular location to repair it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Does it mean that your superior would vacate the premises before you would go there or was it possible for you to see the detainees there?

utterances.speaker: CEDO VULETA
utterances.text: It was not possible for a breakdown to occur in such premises. If a bulb would break down, that wouldn't mean anything in one of such premises.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Did you ever go there to repair any such breakdown or not?

utterances.speaker: CEDO VULETA
utterances.text: No. I never had anything to do in the premises where the detainees were. There was light there, but there were no other installations which would be important for the functioning of the mine in general.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we, therefore, conclude that you were there only to deal with the machinery and the installations which are more complex, if I can put it that way, than a simple lighting system?

utterances.speaker: CEDO VULETA
utterances.text: Yes. I worked on very sophisticated systems such as generators, kitchen installations, refrigerators, furnaces, water wells, pumps at the open pit mine and such like.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] My last question for you, Mr. Vuleta, is of a more general character. In response to a number of questions, you told us that it was not your task, that it was not your job, that you were not interested in learning about that, that this had nothing to do with your competencies and things like that. What was your attitude or, rather, your reaction, your response or maybe your feelings when during those 20 days you were a simple employee of the mine, and once the camp was closed down, you continued working in the mine. During that period of time, many detainees were there, and I would like to know how you felt about it. What were your feelings about the overall situation? I'm not asking your opinion. I would just like to hear something about the way you felt at that time, to describe for us your feelings at that time as a human being.

utterances.speaker: CEDO VULETA
utterances.text: I felt very bad. I don't know how to explain this to you, but it was very hard for me to observe all that. I was not in a position to help people. From time to time I was able to give a piece of bread to someone, but in general, I felt very bad.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can I, therefore, conclude that when you say, "This did not interest me," "This was not part of my work, of my competencies," does that mean that you did not wish to see all that?

utterances.speaker: CEDO VULETA
utterances.text: Well, it's true. I didn't wish to observe such things because it's very difficult for one to observe such terrible things and not being able to help. But those were people who -- there were people there who worked with me, but in general, I really felt very bad.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much, Mr. Vuleta. Thank you for coming here to testify. Unfortunately, I'm not in a position to offer you a glass of brandy. This is not the mission of the Tribunal. But I hope you will be able to go out a little and have a drink. Thank you very much once again, and let me wish you a safe journey back to your place of residence. Let me ask the usher to show you out of the courtroom. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Saxon.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. I have two housekeeping matters to bring to the Trial Chamber's attention. One is the Prosecution would move now for the admission of the document marked 3/1.79, and Ms. Somers has asked me to inform the Trial Chamber that the Prosecution has asked the audiovisual unit for a copy of the B/C/S tape of the testimony this morning because we have -- the Prosecution has a question regarding translation and they want to review the tape. So we may bring a matter to your attention later today.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, but Mr. Saxon, would it be possible to discuss the issue tomorrow during the Status Conference --

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Of course.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] -- so we can move ahead with the witnesses? Thank you, thank you. So it will be part of our agenda tomorrow. Mr. Simic, what's next? MR. K. SIMIC: [Interpretation] The Defence would like to call witness Branko Rosic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Mr. Rosic. Can you hear me?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I can hear you, thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Will you please read the solemn declaration that the usher is going to give to you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You may be seated now, thank you. I am a little bit jealous of your ability to read at such a distance.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much for coming here to testify. First of all you will be answering questions that will be put to you by Mr. Krstan Simic. Mr. Simic, your witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. K
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Mr. Rosic.

utterances.speaker: BRANKO ROSIC
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. K
utterances.text: Together with my colleague Mr. Branko Lukic, on behalf of Mr. Kvocka as his Defence counsel, I should like to ask you a number of questions relating to the incidents that you witnessed.

utterances.speaker: BRANKO ROSIC
utterances.text: Yes, thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. K
utterances.text: For the record, please, would you state your full name and surname?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO ROSIC
utterances.text: My name is Branko Rosic.

utterances.speaker: MR. K
utterances.text: When were you born, Mr. Rosic?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO ROSIC
utterances.text: On the 31st of January, 1936.

utterances.speaker: MR. K
utterances.text: Where were you born?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO ROSIC
utterances.text: In the village of Busnovi.

utterances.speaker: MR. K
utterances.text: In the municipality of Prijedor?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO ROSIC
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. K
utterances.text: Do you still live there?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO ROSIC
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. K
utterances.text: What is your occupation, Mr. Rosic?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO ROSIC
utterances.text: I'm a farmer.

utterances.speaker: MR. K
utterances.text: What did you do before that?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO ROSIC
utterances.text: I used to work in the pump operating company.

utterances.speaker: MR. K
utterances.text: What was the name of your company?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO ROSIC
utterances.text: The name of the company was Ljubija Iron Ore Mine.

utterances.speaker: MR. K
utterances.text: In 1992, were you a military conscript?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO ROSIC
utterances.text: Yes, I was.

utterances.speaker: MR. K
utterances.text: In 1992, did you have a military obligation, and were you deployed anywhere for that purpose?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO ROSIC
utterances.text: I was in my company in the Ljubija Iron Ore Mine.

utterances.speaker: MR. K
utterances.text: Could you be more specific? It's a very general term, "Ljubija Iron Ore Mine."

utterances.speaker: BRANKO ROSIC
utterances.text: There is a location -- there is a facility of that company in Tomasica.

utterances.speaker: MR. K
utterances.text: No, I'm not asking you that. I would like to know where you worked.

utterances.speaker: BRANKO ROSIC
utterances.text: I worked at the open pit pumps.

utterances.speaker: MR. K
utterances.text: Are you referring to the Omarska open pit?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO ROSIC
utterances.text: Yes, I am.

utterances.speaker: MR. K
utterances.text: In May, June, and July 1992, did you have a military assignment in the open pit mine in Omarska?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO ROSIC
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. K
utterances.text: What was your military assignment? How was it organised? How much time would you spend working, for example?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO ROSIC
utterances.text: I would work for 24 hours, and then I would be off duty for 48 hours.

utterances.speaker: MR. K
utterances.text: During that period of time, that is, May, June, July, and August 1992, who was your superior? Who was your boss?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO ROSIC
utterances.text: My boss was Mirko Babic.

utterances.speaker: MR. K
utterances.text: During that period of time, were there any other people who worked on the same kind of assignment as you did?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO ROSIC
utterances.text: Yes, there were.

utterances.speaker: MR. K
utterances.text: Since we have already spoken about the issue in detail, let me just ask you whether Mr. Cedo Vuleta worked there as well?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO ROSIC
utterances.text: Yes, he did.

utterances.speaker: MR. K
utterances.text: We discussed these issues with Mr. Vuleta in detail, so I'm going to focus on one particular incident with you, Mr. Rosic. Did you work in the Omarska mine, that is, in the Omarska open pit in May 1992, that is, on the 30th of May, 1992?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO ROSIC
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. K
utterances.text: Let me repeat the question -- a correction has been made, thank you. Did anyone visit you on that particular day?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO ROSIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. K
utterances.text: Who was it?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO ROSIC
utterances.text: It was my son.

utterances.speaker: MR. K
utterances.text: What was his name?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO ROSIC
utterances.text: My son's name was Milenko.

utterances.speaker: MR. K
utterances.text: Why did he come on that particular day? Why did he look for you?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO ROSIC
utterances.text: He came to see me, to see us, to see what we were doing there.

utterances.speaker: MR. K
utterances.text: Did anything happen on the 30th of May?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO ROSIC
utterances.text: Well, on the 30th of May, there was a war going on in our area.

utterances.speaker: MR. K
utterances.text: Was the town of Prijedor attacked on that day?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO ROSIC
utterances.text: Yes. That was the day of the attack on the town of Prijedor.

utterances.speaker: MR. K
utterances.text: On the 30th of May when you were on duty, when you worked, were any buses coming, coming in with detainees?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO ROSIC
utterances.text: Yes, they were.

utterances.speaker: MR. K
utterances.text: Were there several buses bringing in detainees?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO ROSIC
utterances.text: Yes, there were several of them.

utterances.speaker: MR. K
utterances.text: On that day, Mr. Rosic, did any incident happen during the arrival of one of those buses?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO ROSIC
utterances.text: Yes, it did.

utterances.speaker: MR. K
utterances.text: Could you tell us the time of the day the incident took place?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO ROSIC
utterances.text: It happened sometime in the afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. K
utterances.text: At what time? Do you have any idea at what time?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO ROSIC
utterances.text: Around 3.00, 4.00, or maybe 5.00. I don't know the exact time. I wasn't interested in that.

utterances.speaker: MR. K
utterances.text: Where were you standing at that moment?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO ROSIC
utterances.text: I was standing at the corner of the hangar building on the right-hand side.

utterances.speaker: MR. K
utterances.text: Was your son Milenko with you at the time?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO ROSIC
utterances.text: Yes, he was.

utterances.speaker: MR. K
utterances.text: What were you doing?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO ROSIC
utterances.text: We were talking. My son came to see me, to see how I was doing, what the situation was at my workplace.

utterances.speaker: MR. K
utterances.text: Could you briefly describe for us what happened at that moment?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO ROSIC
utterances.text: People were brought in, in a bus, and they got off the bus. And then there was an inspection of some kind going on, I don't know exactly what they were doing with them, but all of a sudden from behind the bus a soldier appeared. He had a long-barrelled gun. I don't know exactly what kind of rifle it was; I'm not an expert on that. And then he fired -- he started firing on them.

utterances.speaker: MR. K
utterances.text: He started firing on whom?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO ROSIC
utterances.text: Well, on the people who had got off the bus. There was a lot of noise all of a sudden.

utterances.speaker: MR. K
utterances.text: Were people screaming?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO ROSIC
utterances.text: Yes, of course they were screaming. And then at that moment Kvocka came out and he started shouting, "Stop the shooting, you will kill these people." It was Miroslav Kvocka who said that.

utterances.speaker: MR. K
utterances.text: Would you please pause for a moment. Where did Kvocka come from? Were you able to see the house?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO ROSIC
utterances.text: He came from the side, from one of the buildings there. There were a lot of people there, so I was not able to see where he had rushed out from.

utterances.speaker: MR. K
utterances.text: Mr. Rosic, could you describe to us the location where the shooting occurred? You said you were standing at the corner of the hangar, and where exactly was the shooting going on?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO ROSIC
utterances.text: The shooting took place between the administration building and the hangar building, between those two buildings.

utterances.speaker: MR. K
utterances.text: What about the people getting off the bus, where were they being taken to?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO ROSIC
utterances.text: Well, at that point in time, they were not being taken anywhere. They were standing in front of the administration building.

utterances.speaker: MR. K
utterances.text: I have to ask you to pause a little before answering my question because of the interpretation. I'm not referring to the people who had already been shot at but the people who got off the bus, where did they go?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO ROSIC
utterances.text: They went to the building.

utterances.speaker: MR. K
utterances.text: Which building?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO ROSIC
utterances.text: I don't know how to describe that building. It was a kind of building which housed a number of workshops. I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. K
utterances.text: Was it the building which contained the restaurant as well?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO ROSIC
utterances.text: Yes, they were there as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. K
utterances.text: Mr. Rosic, I'm not asking you about the place where people were eventually located or accommodated. I'm trying to see where people were taken before the shooting. We know where they were located, where they were accommodated later on.

utterances.speaker: BRANKO ROSIC
utterances.text: At that moment, they were between those two buildings when they got off the bus. They were standing there and there was some kind of inspection going on.

utterances.speaker: MR. K
utterances.text: When Kvocka appeared, where did he stand in relation to the man who was shooting, in front of him, behind him? Where exactly was he?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO ROSIC
utterances.text: He positioned himself in front of him so that he wouldn't shoot at those people, so that he wouldn't kill them.

utterances.speaker: MR. K
utterances.text: Did Kvocka shelter those people with his body?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO ROSIC
utterances.text: Yes. He spread his arms like this, and he tried to shelter those people.

utterances.speaker: MR. K
utterances.text: Did he try to shelter the people who were being shot at?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO ROSIC
utterances.text: Yes, he did.

utterances.speaker: MR. K
utterances.text: Was he saying anything? Did he shout?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO ROSIC
utterances.text: Yes. He shouted, "Do not shoot. There are people standing there."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Simic, if you want to find out whether Mr. Kvocka -- if you're saying that Mr. Kvocka stood in front of those people in an attempt to shelter them, I think it's a leading question. You should ask what his position was exactly. MR. K. SIMIC: [Interpretation] I accept your suggestion, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. K
utterances.text: What was the position of Mr. Kvocka in relation to the man who opened fire?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO ROSIC
utterances.text: He stood in front of him, in front of his barrel, and he put down the barrel of his gun. Some other people arrived in the meantime and removed the man. They took away his weapon.

utterances.speaker: MR. K
utterances.text: Who did they remove?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO ROSIC
utterances.text: They removed the man who had opened fire.

utterances.speaker: MR. K
utterances.text: On that occasion, were people injured?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO ROSIC
utterances.text: Yes, there were some injuries.

utterances.speaker: MR. K
utterances.text: Were several people injured?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO ROSIC
utterances.text: I don't know exactly, but certainly there must have been. I don't know, I didn't count them, but five or six for sure. There may even have been someone killed.

utterances.speaker: MR. K
utterances.text: Was there any blood on the asphalt, on the road?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO ROSIC
utterances.text: Yes, there was.

utterances.speaker: MR. K
utterances.text: After this person in military uniform was taken away, were any steps taken to assist these people?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO ROSIC
utterances.text: Yes. The ambulance came, a big vehicle and a smaller one with a Red Cross sign. They picked them up and drove them off to the hospital, and they gave them first aid, to those who survived. That's how it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. K
utterances.text: On that occasion, were all the persons who had been hit in this terrible incident driven away?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO ROSIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. K
utterances.text: Did any doctors or nurses appear? Did you notice any?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO ROSIC
utterances.text: There was someone in white coats, but I don't know who they were.

utterances.speaker: MR. K
utterances.text: On that occasion, were you able to see how Mr. Kvocka acted after the shooting?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO ROSIC
utterances.text: After the shooting, Mr. Kvocka, having called for the ambulance to take the people away, after that, after all that, he got into his car and he left.

utterances.speaker: MR. K
utterances.text: Do you know where he went?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO ROSIC
utterances.text: I don't.

utterances.speaker: MR. K
utterances.text: Was the spot where the shooting occurred washed with water?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO ROSIC
utterances.text: Yes, it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. K
utterances.text: Who did the washing? Do you know?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO ROSIC
utterances.text: The women who were engaged there for cleaning purposes and some men too who washed it away and cleaned it up.

utterances.speaker: MR. K
utterances.text: During that shooting incident, were any of the guards injured?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO ROSIC
utterances.text: I don't know that.

utterances.speaker: MR. K
utterances.text: Mr. Rosic, was this a terrible event in your life?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO ROSIC
utterances.text: Of course it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. K
utterances.text: On that occasion, bearing in mind everything that was going on, would you say that Mr. Kvocka demonstrated a great deal of courage?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO ROSIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Objection. Objection, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Yes, Mr. Saxon.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Your Honour, Mr. Simic is now testifying for this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Simic, can you rephrase your question, please. You are aware of the reasons why you need to rephrase it or do you have any reasons why you think you need to keep it as it stands? Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. MR. K. SIMIC: [Interpretation] I see absolutely no reason. I will not put the question again. I think the Chamber will be able to make their own judgement about this incident because there are other witnesses. I have no further questions for this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Otherwise, you are drawing conclusions from the testimony, Mr. Krstan Simic. Mr. Saxon, do you have anything to add? Mr. Simic has said that he would withdraw the question, and he would allow the Chamber to make its own conclusions. He's doing well.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Based on Mr. Simic's willingness to withdraw the question, I have nothing further. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well, then. Mr. Simic, you may continue with your questions. MR. K. SIMIC: [Interpretation] Your Honour, the Defence has no further questions, and accepting your suggestion that Mr. Vuleta has given all the facts to the Chamber regarding the organisation of the camp. So this witness was called simply to testify about this particular fact.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Thank you very much. That was well done, Mr. Simic, I must say. Do any other Defence counsel have any questions? I see they do not. Very well, then. The Prosecution. Mr. Rosic, you're going to answer the questions the Prosecution has for you. Mr. Saxon, your witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Mr. Rosic, is your memory of the events of the day of that shooting at Omarska still pretty clear?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO ROSIC
utterances.text: It is.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: If you know, who was the guard shift leader on duty at the time of the shooting? MR. K. SIMIC: [Interpretation] Objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. Simic. MR. K. SIMIC: [Interpretation] We didn't discuss with the witness at all the existence of shifts or the leaders of shifts. There was no mention of that at all, never mind shift leaders.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Simic, you will have a chance to re-examine the witness. The witness said he was there, Mr. Simic. So continue, please, Mr. Saxon.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Mr. Rosic, I'll repeat my question. The question was, if you know: Who was the guard shift leader on duty at the time of the shooting?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO ROSIC
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Approximately how many buses were standing there or parked there close to the administration building when the shooting began?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO ROSIC
utterances.text: I don't know the exact number. I didn't count them.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Could you give an estimate?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO ROSIC
utterances.text: There were several for sure, but I don't know exactly. Maybe ten or -- I don't know exactly. I didn't count them. Maybe as many as 20.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: You mentioned that you were standing by one corner of the hangar building and you were speaking with your son Milenko.

utterances.speaker: BRANKO ROSIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Do you recall if there were any guards present either on the pista, around the buses, near the prisoners who were getting off the buses, anywhere around?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO ROSIC
utterances.text: There were some, only I don't know them. I don't know who they were.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Yes. Can you estimate approximately how many guards were there?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO ROSIC
utterances.text: I don't know exactly, but there must have been five or six of them, maybe more. I didn't actually register how many there were.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Were these guards armed?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO ROSIC
utterances.text: They were.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Do you recall what kind of arms they had?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO ROSIC
utterances.text: I don't remember the kind of weapons they had.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: But they were firearms, yes? They were guns for shooting?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO ROSIC
utterances.text: Firearms, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Do you recall approximately where these five or six armed guards were standing just before the shooting began?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO ROSIC
utterances.text: They were standing somewhere around those buses in front of the building, between the two buildings. There are two buildings there, you see.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Yes. So the guards and the buses and the prisoners were located on that asphalt area that's between the large hangar building and the building where the restaurant is located; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO ROSIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Would you agree with me that to walk across that asphalt area from the restaurant building to the wall of the hangar building, it's a pretty short distance, only about 50 or 60 steps?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO ROSIC
utterances.text: Well, yes, that is the distance, as you say.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: When the man with the long-barrelled rifle began shooting, where was that man standing?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO ROSIC
utterances.text: He was standing in front of the men who were being inspected to see what they had on them. I don't know exactly what they were doing. He was standing in front of them. He came there.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: You mentioned that the guards had firearms, and you mentioned that after the shooting began, Miroslav Kvocka appeared. Was Mr. Kvocka armed that day?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO ROSIC
utterances.text: He had a pistol.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Now, you said that the prisoners, before the shooting began, as you put it, they had left the buses and they were being inspected. When you say they were being inspected, do you mean searched?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO ROSIC
utterances.text: They were being searched, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And did you observe some of these prisoners being searched before the shooting began?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO ROSIC
utterances.text: I didn't. I wasn't so close to be able to watch the way they were being searched. I was some distance away.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Well, you were less than 50 steps away; is that right?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO ROSIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: From where you were standing, could you see if those prisoners standing outside the buses were being treated correctly?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO ROSIC
utterances.text: I think they were. I didn't notice anything as they were getting off the buses. I saw that. I saw that just then they were treating them decently.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Now, when the shooting began, you said a number of prisoners were killed -- were wounded, I'm sorry, and one or more may have been killed. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO ROSIC
utterances.text: It is.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Did you know Miroslav Kvocka before this incident?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO ROSIC
utterances.text: I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: How did you know Mr. Kvocka?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO ROSIC
utterances.text: I knew him. He was in our district, an ordinary policeman, and that is how I knew him, in the police station.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Mr. Kvocka is an intelligent man, isn't he?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO ROSIC
utterances.text: He is.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: He's a professional police officer, or he was at that time, wasn't he?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO ROSIC
utterances.text: He was a professional policeman as far as I know.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Mr. Rosic, when the shooting began, what did Miroslav Kvocka do with his pistol?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO ROSIC
utterances.text: I don't know that.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Mr. Kvocka could have fired his pistol at the man with the long-barrelled rifle, couldn't he?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO ROSIC
utterances.text: He could have, but he didn't open fire. I didn't see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Mr. Kvocka could have struck the man with the long-barrelled rifle with his weapon, couldn't he?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO ROSIC
utterances.text: He could have, but he didn't do that. I didn't see him do that. He just shouted out, "Don't shoot. You're killing people."

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And when Mr. Kvocka made that statement, Mr. Kvocka didn't indicate which persons he was referring to, did he?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO ROSIC
utterances.text: I don't know that. I'm afraid I don't understand what you mean.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: I'll move on. Would you agree with me, Mr. Rosic, that it would have been easier and safer for Mr. Kvocka to have disarmed -- MR. K. SIMIC: [Interpretation] Objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. Simic. MR. K. SIMIC: [Interpretation] My learned friend is asking for an assessment as to what would have happened if such a thing had happened, a hypothetical: A policeman could have done this or that. He stood in front of the barrel to prevent people being killed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Saxon, I think Mr. Simic is right. What is your reply?

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: My reply first of all, Your Honour, is that I have not finished asking my question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Okay. But perhaps you could move a little faster to get to your question; otherwise, we're asking the witness, could he have done this, could he have done that. So please proceed and put your question to the witness. Perhaps we'll be able to understand better once you do.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Mr. Rosic, could Mr. Kvocka have used his pistol to disarm the man with the long-barrelled gun?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO ROSIC
utterances.text: He could have, but that is what -- but that is something he didn't do as far as I was able to see.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Neither the guards who were present nor Mr. Kvocka raised their weapon nor fired their weapon at the man who was shooting; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO ROSIC
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: If you know, why didn't Miroslav Kvocka or the guards shoot the man who was firing his weapon and injuring prisoners? MR. K. SIMIC: [Interpretation] Objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Simic, you were going to say? Say, please. MR. K. SIMIC: [Interpretation] This is pure speculation. The witness is asked to speculate.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] For a moment I asked you whether that was logical or not. The witness can answer. The question is: Do you know why Mr. Kvocka and the guards did not use their arms to disarm this man? The witness can say, because - I'm not going to lead, anyway - because the soldier who was shooting had colleagues, they were stronger than them. So you see, there can always be a good logic and a bad logic. At first sight, you may be right to raise an objection, but if we go deeper into the issue, then perhaps there is no justification for the objection. So I'm going to allow the Prosecutor to put his question, but I owed you an explanation as to why I think the Prosecutor should put his question. But there are other situations when I shall simply say "overruled," so I'm warning you. Mr. Saxon, please continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Mr. Rosic, if you know, do you know why Miroslav Kvocka or the armed guards who were present did not shoot the man who began to fire?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO ROSIC
utterances.text: I don't know that.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Once the shooting began, a number of detainees, prisoners, were immediately wounded or perhaps killed, right?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO ROSIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: If Mr. Kvocka had placed himself in the line of fire, he would have been shot as well?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO ROSIC
utterances.text: That should be right, but I don't know. It wasn't up to me to decide anything.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: So Mr. Rosic, Mr. Kvocka never placed himself in the line of fire, did he? MR. K. SIMIC: [Interpretation] Your Honour, objection.

utterances.speaker: BRANKO ROSIC
utterances.text: He did place himself in the line of fire when he stood in front of the long barrel and said, "Stop shooting these men." That is what Kvocka did. I saw that. MR. K. SIMIC: [Interpretation] Your Honour, the time has long since expired.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Your Honour, may I respond to that last comment?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, if you can, quickly.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: I believe the direct examination took about half an hour, and I believe I've used about 22 minutes on cross-examination. So I'm just honestly confused by Mr. Simic's comment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We can't laugh here. We're doing a serious job. I think Mr. Simic is trying to destabilise you, but you're not going to let him do it, so please continue. Let me look at the translation. Well translated. So you may continue, please, Mr. Saxon.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Mr. Rosic, can you recall how much time went by between the shooting of the prisoners and when the wounded persons were actually taken away?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO ROSIC
utterances.text: I don't know exactly how much time could have passed, but they were taken away quite quickly.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: You mentioned that some women were -- I believe you mentioned that some women washed the blood off the asphalt on the pista area. Do you know who told those women to wash the blood away?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO ROSIC
utterances.text: I don't know that.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Mr. Rosic, did you work at the Omarska camp during May, June, July, and August of 1992?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO ROSIC
utterances.text: I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Apart from this shooting incident on the 30th of May, how often did you see Mr. Kvocka there?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO ROSIC
utterances.text: I saw him a couple of times more. Not too many. Maybe several times.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: In 1992, did you know a man named Dragoljub Prcac?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO ROSIC
utterances.text: I did know him, by sight.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: During the summer of 1992, did you ever see Dragoljub Prcac at the Omarska camp?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO ROSIC
utterances.text: I didn't know him that well to be able to really say that I saw him. I didn't know him very well. We didn't have much contact. I didn't really know him at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: I'm trying to make sure that I understand your response, so please bear with me. Are you saying that you never saw Dragoljub Prcac at the Omarska camp or that you did see him there but you never had any personal contact with Mr. Prcac at the Omarska camp?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO ROSIC
utterances.text: I had no contact, but I did see him there. For a while I saw him there as an individual.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Approximately when was the first time that you saw Dragoljub Prcac at the Omarska camp?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO ROSIC
utterances.text: I don't remember that, I'm afraid, when that was.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Do you know what Dragoljub Prcac's duties or responsibilities were at the Omarska camp?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO ROSIC
utterances.text: I don't know that either.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: I ask the Court's indulgence for one moment, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Your Honour, at this time, I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much, Mr. Saxon. Mr. Simic, any re-examination? MR. K. SIMIC: [Interpretation] Just one question.

utterances.speaker: MR. K
utterances.text: Mr. Rosic, how long did this shooting, this incident, this chaotic situation go on for? Was it an hour?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO ROSIC
utterances.text: No. It was brief. I didn't check the time to be able to tell you, but it was over in a couple of minutes. The man was prevented from continuing and removed and that was all. MR. K. SIMIC: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much, Mr. Simic. Judge Fouad Riad, do you have any questions?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Judge Wald? No. So we have no questions for you Mr. Rosic. You have just completed your testimony here. Thank you very much for coming, and we wish you a safe journey home. I'm going to ask the usher to accompany you out.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So Mr. Krstan Simic, would you like to have a lunch break? Would that suit you? MR. K. SIMIC: [Interpretation] Yes, indeed, Your Honour. It would suit me exceptionally.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well, then. So we're going to have a 50-minute break now. --- Luncheon recess taken at 1.00 p.m.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You may be seated. Mr. Simic, Krstan Simic. MR. K. SIMIC: [Interpretation] Your Honours, the Defence calls witness Milenko Rosic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Mr. Milenko Rosic. Can you hear me?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon. Yes, I can hear you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Will you please read the solemn declaration that the usher is going to give to you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You may be seated.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Would you please come closer to the microphone so that we can hear you. You will first be answering questions that Mr. Simic is going to put to you. Mr. Simic, your witness. MR. K. SIMIC: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. K
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Once again, good afternoon, Mr. Rosic.

utterances.speaker: MILENKO ROSIC
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. K
utterances.text: On behalf of the Defence team of Mr. Kvocka, I should like to ask a few questions of you relating to the events that you witnessed.

utterances.speaker: MILENKO ROSIC
utterances.text: Please do.

utterances.speaker: MR. K
utterances.text: However, before that, for the record, would you please state your name and surname?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO ROSIC
utterances.text: Milenko Rosic.

utterances.speaker: MR. K
utterances.text: Mr. Rosic, when were you born?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO ROSIC
utterances.text: On the 28th of March, 1962.

utterances.speaker: MR. K
utterances.text: Where were you born?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO ROSIC
utterances.text: In the village of Busnovi in the municipality of Prijedor.

utterances.speaker: MR. K
utterances.text: What is the name of your father?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO ROSIC
utterances.text: Branko.

utterances.speaker: MR. K
utterances.text: Where do you live today?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO ROSIC
utterances.text: I live in Banja Luka, in Maricka Kovackavica street, house number ten.

utterances.speaker: MR. K
utterances.text: What is your profession?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO ROSIC
utterances.text: I work in the catering business. I graduated from a catering school, and I have two such businesses in Banja Luka.

utterances.speaker: MR. K
utterances.text: Are you married?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO ROSIC
utterances.text: Yes, I am.

utterances.speaker: MR. K
utterances.text: Do have you any children?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO ROSIC
utterances.text: I have two children.

utterances.speaker: MR. K
utterances.text: Where and when did you do your military service?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO ROSIC
utterances.text: From the 8th of April, 1981, in Ljubljana.

utterances.speaker: MR. K
utterances.text: How long did you stay in the army?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO ROSIC
utterances.text: Until the 8th of June, 1982 [Realtime transcript read in error "1992"].

utterances.speaker: MR. K
utterances.text: Mr. Rosic, how long have you been living in Banja Luka?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO ROSIC
utterances.text: Since 1982.

utterances.speaker: MR. K
utterances.text: There seems to be a mistake in the transcript regarding the date Mr. Rosic left the army. The record reads "1992." What exactly did you say, Mr. Rosic?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO ROSIC
utterances.text: The 8th of June, 1982.

utterances.speaker: MR. K
utterances.text: It's been corrected now. During the month of May, did you ever visit your parents?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO ROSIC
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. K
utterances.text: On the 30th of May, did you go to see your parents?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO ROSIC
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. K
utterances.text: Do you remember the reason for that particular visit?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO ROSIC
utterances.text: Yes, I do. I can tell you right away what the reason was. It was because of the attack on Prijedor. The attack took place in the early morning hours, and I heard about it on the radio and TV.

utterances.speaker: MR. K
utterances.text: What year was that?

utterances.speaker: MR. K
utterances.text: Where did you go?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO ROSIC
utterances.text: First of all, I went to my parents' house in the village of Busnovi.

utterances.speaker: MR. K
utterances.text: Who did you find there?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO ROSIC
utterances.text: I found only my mother there.

utterances.speaker: MR. K
utterances.text: What did she tell you about the whereabouts of your father at that time?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO ROSIC
utterances.text: My father was at work. He was discharging his work obligation in the mine where he was an employee.

utterances.speaker: MR. K
utterances.text: So from there, from that house, did you go to see your father?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO ROSIC
utterances.text: First of all, I went to see my sisters because I have two sisters living there. Then in the afternoon of the same day, I went to see my father.

utterances.speaker: MR. K
utterances.text: Where did you find him?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO ROSIC
utterances.text: I found my father within the Omarska mine compound. That is on the way to my father's house.

utterances.speaker: MR. K
utterances.text: At the entrance to the compound was there any security?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO ROSIC
utterances.text: There was a guard there, a janitor, I believe, and a reserve policeman. There was a janitor there who was an employee of the mine.

utterances.speaker: MR. K
utterances.text: Did you have any problems entering the facility on the 30th of May, 1992?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO ROSIC
utterances.text: I wanted them to call my father because he was an employee there and everybody knew him. So they told me to continue further on some 100 metres away from there towards the hangar because he was there. I didn't have any major difficulties getting there.

utterances.speaker: MR. K
utterances.text: Did you indeed find your father there?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO ROSIC
utterances.text: Yes, I did. He was in the hangar, and he came out of the hangar, and we were standing there in the compound.

utterances.speaker: MR. K
utterances.text: Can you remember where exactly it was where you talked to your father in relation to the administration building and the hangar?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO ROSIC
utterances.text: It was at the very entrance to the hangar where some dumpers were parked, at the corner of the building, perhaps a couple of metres away from the corner of the hangar. I don't know how else to put it. At the corner of the hangar where the pista was, and right across was the administration building.

utterances.speaker: MR. K
utterances.text: Mr. Rosic, did anything unusual happen at that time? Were there any buses there?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO ROSIC
utterances.text: There was one or maybe two buses that were there at the moment, as far as I can remember. Some people were getting off the bus between the hangar and this other building. There was a kind of passage there, an open space.

utterances.speaker: MR. K
utterances.text: Did you pay attention to the people who were getting off?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO ROSIC
utterances.text: Not very much, because I was interested in what was happening with my father.

utterances.speaker: MR. K
utterances.text: On that occasion, were people who were getting off being searched? Did you see anything like that?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO ROSIC
utterances.text: Yes, there were searches going on as people were getting off the bus, but at that moment, I didn't know what was going on.

utterances.speaker: MR. K
utterances.text: Did your father tell you anything about where the buses were coming from?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO ROSIC
utterances.text: He told me that it was a consequence of what was happening in Prijedor, that those people were some kind of prisoners and that the area was some kind of centre for them. But it was the very beginning, and he Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. himself didn't know what was actually going on.

utterances.speaker: MR. K
utterances.text: Did he say anything about the fact that there had been other buses on that day?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO ROSIC
utterances.text: Yes. He told me that about ten buses had already arrived with some people, but at the moment when I was there, there was only one or maybe two buses there.

utterances.speaker: MR. K
utterances.text: Did he say anything about the fact that there were detainees on those buses?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO ROSIC
utterances.text: He told me that they were detainees, but they were all wearing civilian clothes. So I don't know. They must have been prisoners of some kind.

utterances.speaker: MR. K
utterances.text: While you were talking to your father at the corner of the hangar building -- let me rephrase the question. How far was the spot where you were from the place where the bus had stopped?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO ROSIC
utterances.text: The distance was between 20 and 30 metres, perhaps 25 metres.

utterances.speaker: MR. K
utterances.text: Were there any other persons, in addition to those detainees, wearing uniforms?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO ROSIC
utterances.text: There were people wearing both police and military uniforms, although I wasn't paying any special attention to them.

utterances.speaker: MR. K
utterances.text: Can you remember how many people in military and police uniforms were there at the time, approximately?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO ROSIC
utterances.text: Up to ten individuals, as far as I could see.

utterances.speaker: MR. K
utterances.text: Did anything unusual happen at that moment?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO ROSIC
utterances.text: Yes, a shooting occurred.

utterances.speaker: MR. K
utterances.text: Did you see who opened fire?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO ROSIC
utterances.text: Yes, I did. It was an individual wearing a military uniform. He opened fire in the direction of the civilians.

utterances.speaker: MR. K
utterances.text: So we have this incident; you were there. Could you see where that person appeared from? Could you tell that from the position where you were?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO ROSIC
utterances.text: Yes, I could, but not very precisely.

utterances.speaker: MR. K
utterances.text: Where did he come from?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO ROSIC
utterances.text: He came from the swing gate near the administration building, because that was the only space that he could use, the only way he could use to come there. As to when exactly he emerged from that location, I don't know. I didn't pay any attention to that.

utterances.speaker: MR. K
utterances.text: Could you hear any voices before the shooting?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO ROSIC
utterances.text: At that moment I heard some noise, and then I heard the shooting, the fire that was opened by that person, and at that moment panic occurred and the situation became chaotic.

utterances.speaker: MR. K
utterances.text: What do you mean by that?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO ROSIC
utterances.text: I mean that people were screaming, shouting, falling around. It was a very ugly sight; for me, it was. It was the first time in my life that I found myself in such a situation.

utterances.speaker: MR. K
utterances.text: Did anyone react to what was happening, to the shooting?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO ROSIC
utterances.text: There was a policeman who reacted first. He jumped there and he stood in front of the person who was shooting.

utterances.speaker: MR. K
utterances.text: How do you know that the individual in question was a policeman?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO ROSIC
utterances.text: He was wearing a police uniform.

utterances.speaker: MR. K
utterances.text: Was he armed?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO ROSIC
utterances.text: I think he only had a pistol.

utterances.speaker: MR. K
utterances.text: You just mentioned an individual who jumped in front of the person who was opening fire. Could you describe this for us in greater detail?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO ROSIC
utterances.text: The situation was chaotic, and an individual came out. He rushed to the person who was shooting. He shouted out. He stood in front of him. He spread his arms wide open, and then he shouted -- I don't know whether I can quote his words, but he said something to the effect, "Do not shoot. These are people here. You will kill them." The individual then with the gun stopped firing his weapon, and the policeman took his gun. He put it down, and then other individuals who were there, other soldiers - I don't know who they were - rushed at this individual who was opening fire. Then they started arguing, but they eventually removed the person away, and they took him behind the building, but I don't know the exact location where they took him.

utterances.speaker: MR. K
utterances.text: When the policeman put down the rifle of the individual who was firing, was the individual in question then disarmed? Was his rifle taken away?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO ROSIC
utterances.text: It was only after other policemen had gathered that his rifle was taken away.

utterances.speaker: MR. K
utterances.text: Had you ever seen the individual who was shooting prior to that?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO ROSIC
utterances.text: No, I had not.

utterances.speaker: MR. K
utterances.text: Did you know the person who stopped him?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO ROSIC
utterances.text: No, though my father told me that the name of the person, of the policeman, was Kvocka.

utterances.speaker: MR. K
utterances.text: Did his father tell you how he knew him?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO ROSIC
utterances.text: He knew him because he used to patrol in his village, in the village where my father lived and worked.

utterances.speaker: MR. K
utterances.text: There seems to be an error in the transcript, so let me repeat the question. What did your father tell you, who was it?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO ROSIC
utterances.text: My father told me that it was Kvocka, a policeman.

utterances.speaker: MR. K
utterances.text: Thank you very much. We just needed to correct the record. Were you able to see how many people were injured on that occasion in that chaotic situation, as you say?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO ROSIC
utterances.text: There were many people lying around. There was blood on the pista, because the ambulance arrived only 15 or 20 minutes later on. There was chaos there. I didn't want to come closer to them, so I don't know how many people were lying there on the ground or how many people were injured. I don't know that.

utterances.speaker: MR. K
utterances.text: Could you give us an estimate? Were there several people?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO ROSIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. K
utterances.text: When the ambulance arrived, could you tell us what kind of vehicle it was?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO ROSIC
utterances.text: One of the vehicles was a civilian ambulance vehicle. A man came out of that vehicle. I knew that man personally. And the other vehicle was a very big military vehicle with a red cross on it, but the colour of the vehicle was olive drab.

utterances.speaker: MR. K
utterances.text: When the ambulance arrived, were the injured people helped in any way? Were any measures taken?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO ROSIC
utterances.text: The same policeman who prevented the shooting ran to the building. He called the ambulance. He started shouting at the people around. He wanted the people to be helped, assistance to be provided to them. I tried to keep aside. I didn't want to meddle in that situation.

utterances.speaker: MR. K
utterances.text: The individuals who were victims of this shooting, were they taken away? Did anyone remain on the spot?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO ROSIC
utterances.text: No. They were all taken away.

utterances.speaker: MR. K
utterances.text: Let me go back to this man who jumped at the man who was shooting and who prevented the shooting. The policeman who did it, did he protect those people who were being shot at with his body?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO ROSIC
utterances.text: Yes, literally. He risked being shot at as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. K
utterances.text: Once the bodies were taken away, did you stay there after that?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO ROSIC
utterances.text: For about five or ten minutes more.

utterances.speaker: MR. K
utterances.text: Was the area washed down, the area where the indent occurred?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO ROSIC
utterances.text: Yes. Some people in uniform washed down the area with water hoses. Some women were there as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. K
utterances.text: Did you have an opportunity to see the man who came between the rifle and the crowd of people? What did he look like?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO ROSIC
utterances.text: He looked very scared. I should even say that he looked panicky because it was a very dangerous situation. But he was the one who organised everything, who organised the arrival of the ambulance and the transport of the injured people from there.

utterances.speaker: MR. K
utterances.text: Other policemen who were present there and other soldiers, what did they look like?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO ROSIC
utterances.text: They seemed to be completely lost, like myself.

utterances.speaker: MR. K
utterances.text: Did you see what happened to the policeman afterwards?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO ROSIC
utterances.text: Once the ambulance left, he went to the area behind the administration building, went into a car and left. I don't know where he went.

utterances.speaker: MR. K
utterances.text: How long after that did you leave?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO ROSIC
utterances.text: Some five or ten minutes after that.

utterances.speaker: MR. K
utterances.text: What was the impression that was left on your father by that incident?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO ROSIC
utterances.text: It was a shock for all of us. It was, for us, the first time in our lives that we saw something like that, and my father insisted that I should go home right away.

utterances.speaker: MR. K
utterances.text: Later on, did you visit your father in Omarska again?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO ROSIC
utterances.text: Very rarely. I went to visit him at home.

utterances.speaker: MR. K
utterances.text: Did you ever come into the compound again, camp compound?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO ROSIC
utterances.text: No. Not as long as the camp was there.

utterances.speaker: MR. K
utterances.text: You don't know the policeman personally, do you?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO ROSIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. K
utterances.text: And you didn't get to know him afterwards?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO ROSIC
utterances.text: I saw him on television, the trial on television.

utterances.speaker: MR. K
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Rosic. MR. K. SIMIC: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I have no further questions for this witness.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You're welcome.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. Simic. What about the other Defence counsel? Any questions? I see that there are not. Mr. Saxon, please. Mr. Rosic, you will now be answering questions put to you by the Prosecution, and in this case it is Mr. Saxon who will be asking you the questions. Please continue, Mr. Saxon.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Mr. Rosic, you mentioned that before this shooting began, there were approximately ten individuals standing in that open area, some wearing police uniforms and others wearing military uniforms.

utterances.speaker: MILENKO ROSIC
utterances.text: That's right, about ten. Whether there were eight, ten, or 12, I can't say exactly, but approximately ten.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Were these persons also bearing firearms?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO ROSIC
utterances.text: Some, yes; some, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: You said that the persons who were getting off the bus were being searched as they were getting off the bus. Were you able to observe the kind of treatment the persons getting off the bus were receiving?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO ROSIC
utterances.text: What I was able to see -- as far as I was able to see, their conduct was proper.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Just so the record is clear, when you say, "Their conduct was proper," who are you referring to?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO ROSIC
utterances.text: The individuals performing the search of the civilians.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: You said that when the shooting began, it was a chaotic situation but this policeman reacted first. Where did this policeman come from?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO ROSIC
utterances.text: The first person to react was one policeman, one particular policeman, and after he got hold of the barrel, all the other policemen came up to him.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Was that first policeman who reacted, was he present in that open area before the shooting began?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO ROSIC
utterances.text: He rushed up from the direction of the administration building, and he was some 10 to 20 metres away. I can't tell you exactly. But I noticed him at the arrival, as he ran up.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: You said, and this is from page 82 of the transcript, you said that the individual rushed to the person who was shooting, he shouted, and he stood in front of him.

utterances.speaker: MILENKO ROSIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Mr. Rosic, if you stand in front of someone who is shooting a firearm, don't you usually get shot?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO ROSIC
utterances.text: Yes, but he stopped shooting.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: So help us understand this. A person came to that open area with a gun. What did that person do?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO ROSIC
utterances.text: The person opened fire on this mass of civilians standing there.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Did the person opening fire say anything?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO ROSIC
utterances.text: Well, there were some swear words being bandied about, which I didn't understand. I didn't hear them, actually, properly.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Approximately how long did this --

utterances.speaker: MILENKO ROSIC
utterances.text: And there was someone -- the person was hurt and crying. I can't remember the exact words.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Let's go a little bit more slowly. Approximately how long did the shooting go on for?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO ROSIC
utterances.text: Just a few seconds.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: In those few seconds, approximately how many people were wounded or killed?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO ROSIC
utterances.text: I don't know how many, but there were several people lying down and screaming and crying out.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Were you dressed in civilian clothes at the time?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO ROSIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: You were not shot at the time, were you?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO ROSIC
utterances.text: No, because I was standing to the left by the hangar with my father, and everybody knew my father.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Are you telling the Trial Chamber that the person who came to the Omarska camp that day who did the shooting knew your father?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO ROSIC
utterances.text: No, I can't say that they knew my father, but I wasn't in this mass of civilians, this group of civilians. I was separated, 20 to 30 metres away from the civilian group.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: You did not know the man who was shooting, did you?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO ROSIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Now, you said that when the shooting was over, the people were lying wounded on the ground, the people were screaming. You said that the same policeman who stopped the shooting ran around, shouted to people. He wanted people to be helped. He said and I'm quoting you, "He organised everything. He organised the transport from there," and I take it you mean the transport of the wounded people from Omarska camp. Would it be fair to say then that this policeman took charge of the situation? MR. K. SIMIC: [Interpretation] Objection.

utterances.speaker: MILENKO ROSIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Simic, the witness has already answered. You have your answer, Mr. Prosecutor. You may continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Well, can you clarify this, please? Because in your direct examination you said, and you were referring to this heroic policeman, you said he organised everything. He organised the transport from there. He shouted to people around him. Isn't that the behaviour of someone who was taking control of the situation?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Prosecutor, you should ask the witness what he observed which led him to conclude that this person organised matters. I think you mentioned the departure transport to the hospital. I think that is your question. So you should put it differently; otherwise, you're asking a leading question, Mr. Saxon. So rephrase that, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: I will rephrase my question, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Please go ahead, do so.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: You said that this heroic policeman organised everything. What specifically did he do? MR. K. SIMIC: [Interpretation] Objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Simic. MR. K. SIMIC: [Interpretation] Your Honours, my learned colleague put me right a moment ago when I interpreted the testimony of the witness. The witness said that in this situation of chaos, the policeman who was there had showed the greatest presence of mind in that situation and took steps to help the people. What he said was that he showed presence of mind, was the one to show most presence of mind.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: May I respond to that, Your Honour?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Your Honour, I quoted the English translation verbatim. The English translation said that this witness said he organised everything. He organised the transport from there. So I'm not misleading anyone's testimony, and my question was a very simple one: What did he organise? What did he do?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, we often encounter this problem of the nuances in interpretation, so one should go a step backwards and ask the witness whether he can confirm what he said. If he says he said it that way with precisely those words, then you may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Mr. Rosic, did you not say on direct examination that this heroic policeman, "He organised everything. He organised the transport from there?" Wasn't that your testimony a few minutes ago?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO ROSIC
utterances.text: Let me repeat what I said. The person who showed most presence of mind shouted, asked them to call the ambulance, asked people to help the people. He ran all over trying to do this. Now, you can interpret that any way you like.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Your Honour, I don't think we have a problem with nuances in the translation, and I will stand by my question, but I will move on.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Mr. Rosic, what is your ethnicity?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO ROSIC
utterances.text: I'm a Serb.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And before your testimony today, did you discuss your testimony with Defence counsel?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO ROSIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Did you discuss your testimony with your father?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO ROSIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
